before: A successful deletion may use status 204, which has no response body. A missing record can use a different status under the chosen API contract.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
The conditional expression selects the status and body together. null here models the absence of a body; a real adapter must not serialize the word null into a 204 response.

Read the function call deleteReply(true) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, deleteReply runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
Should the real HTTP adapter send the JSON text null for the 204 branch? The helper uses null as a model marker. HTTP 204 means there is no response content.
after: A response status is a number describing what happened to a request. This rule uses 204 when a record was removed successfully. 204 means success with no response content.
A response body holds content sent back to the caller. A real 204 response has no body. In this small model, body: null marks that absence.
When removed is false, this API's rule returns 404 with an error message of Not found. The ? and : choose the status and body together.
The function creates a JavaScript description of the reply. Code that sends the real HTTP response must turn the 204 case into an empty body. It must not send the JSON text null as its content.
Complete deleteReply(removed). For true, return status 204 with the no-body marker. For false, return status 404 with {error: "Not found"}.
